meta.name: Songhealth CMS Content Model
meta.description: Feature 002 seed intent for the existing canonical platform: defines the shared native documents collection (required title and native file selection, optional domain metadata and the document_successor self-relation), the native pages collection for general information (required title, optional summary and portable-text body, no conditional media fields yet) bound to the optional page_documents relation (Page parent → Document, many-to-many), the native news collection for time-oriented public-information stories (required title, optional summary, portable-text body, featured image and source text, no speculative relations), the native activities collection for activity/meeting/field-work/event records (required title, optional summary, native offset-aware activity datetime distinct from native publication/scheduling time, location text, featured image, gallery repeater of image rows with optional captions preserving array order, and external participants kept as text — no separate participant/place identities or speculative relations), the native announcements collection for official notices (required title, optional portable-text details, native offset-aware announcement/opening/closing domain datetimes distinct from native publication/scheduling time, and optional related documents bound to the announcement_documents relation — Announcement parent → Document, many-to-many, no date-driven automatic unpublish), the native health_content collection for evergreen health-knowledge guidance (required title, optional summary, portable-text body, source text, featured image and native offset-aware reviewed_at/next_review_at domain datetimes distinct from native publication/scheduling time, with no review-date-driven automatic unpublish), the native services collection for citizen-service guidance (required title; optional summary, ownership_type select preserving the four approved direct/coordinated/related_health_service/external_digital meanings, provider text, channel repeater rows with optional label string and optional native url, eligibility/steps/required-documents/contact-location portable-text guidance, duration/fees/notes text and external url — editorial guidance only, with no transaction, payment or attachment engine) bound to the optional service_documents relation (Service parent → Document, many-to-many with unlimited maxima), and the native health_reports collection for health-report metadata describing one selected authoritative Document (required title; optional summary, reporting period, owner/source, native offset-aware report datetime distinct from native publication/scheduling time and fiscal year — explanatory metadata only, with no analytical metrics, dataset or extra publication rule) appended to shared topic and hierarchical area with the Report-only report_type classification. T017 defines that mandatory single report_document reference: the seed declares the report_document relation (Health Report parent → Document, one child maximum per Report and unlimited Report parents per Document) and explicitly binds the Report's report_document reference field with native top-level required true on the parent side, so automatic field-created relation naming cannot introduce a duplicate edge set and the Document selection stays in the separate native references payload rather than data; schema application and runtime verification remain separate scope and are not claimed here. T028 adds the native health_services collection for real health-service facilities, not an HIS (required official-name title; optional facility code, display name, operational-status select preserving the approved active/temporarily_closed/inactive values, address text, latitude/longitude numbers under the native inclusive −90..90 and −180..180 coordinate ranges, opening-hours and public-contact text, affiliation owner text per the accepted T025 Organization N/A disposition, and facility image), with physical address/coordinates distinct from service-coverage area selection, no Organization links (the conditional Organization stays unactivated), and no records, terms, facility codes or inventories populated. T029 declares the single reciprocal facility_services relation (Health Service parent → Service, many-to-many with unlimited maxima on both ends and no duplicate reverse relation) and explicitly binds its two optional selectors over that one edge set — health_services.offered_services on the parent side and services.offering_facilities on the child side, both non-required so empty selections remain valid and automatic field-created relation naming cannot introduce a second edge set — preserving native staged/live reciprocal semantics with no backlink index, custom adapter or availability constraint; schema application and runtime verification remain separate scope and are not claimed here. The shared native taxonomies remain topic, audience and hierarchical area — plus the Document-only document_type, News-only news_category, Announcement-only announcement_type, Service-only service_category, Report-only report_type and Health-Service-only facility_type classifications, with topic attached to documents, news, activities, announcements, health_content, services and health_reports, document_type to documents, news_category to news, announcement_type to announcements, service_category to services, report_type to health_reports, facility_type to health_services, audience attached to news, announcements, health_content and services, and area attached to news, activities, health_reports and health_services. Still defines zero menus, redirects, widgetAreas, sections and content, suppressing EmDash's built-in example Posts/Pages model. Term inventories are intentionally empty pending authoritative sources; no official terms, geographic codes or inventories are supplied. Taxonomy attachments are added as each owning collection is introduced. Area terms model the applicable Province → District → Subdistrict → Village hierarchy: explicit official/stable code in the native term slug, name in the native label, parent via native group identity.
